dynamic_headline: Fed/rates leads a constructive but selective pre-market setup.
market_summary: The pre-market setup is constructive but selective, based on 1642 articles from Yahoo Finance, TradingView, Investing.com, The Motley Fool, 24/7 Wall St.. The dominant theme is macro, with 684 macro items, 526 company items, 385 industry items, and 47 policy items. The tape looks more useful for identifying near-term rotation and risk appetite than for making a single directional index call.
market_narrative: US equities have a constructive but selective bias as Fed/rates, oil/energy, inflation dominate the information flow. Before the open, the setup still needs confirmation from futures, Treasury yields, opening breadth and pre-market volume.
index_performance_summary: Nasdaq and growth indexes should be the most sensitive part of the tape when AI, semiconductor, mega-cap tech, or guidance stories dominate. S&P 500 direction is likely to remain tied to Treasury yields, Fed expectations, inflation data, and broad risk appetite. Dow and equal-weight exposure may react more to policy, regulation, tariff, and industrial-cycle headlines.
macro_outlook: Macro coverage is concentrated around Fed/rates (235), oil/energy (101), inflation (97), growth/jobs (22). The practical implication is that equity rallies may need confirmation from rates and inflation expectations; if yields rise while growth headlines weaken, risk appetite can fade quickly.
risk_and_sentiment: Sentiment is constructive but selective: 238 positive, 155 negative, and 1249 neutral articles. My read is to avoid treating headline volume as conviction by itself; the more important signal is whether macro-sensitive and technology-sensitive stories are pointing in the same direction.
